title: Embedded Systems and IoT Engineer
summary: Embedded engineers write the firmware that runs on microcontrollers inside devices, and IoT engineers connect those devices to networks. This path suits students who enjoy both code and hardware: C, microcontrollers, an RTOS, communication protocols and embedded Linux.

sources.title: Introduction to Embedded System Design – NPTEL

nodes.title: C for embedded systems
nodes.summary: C is the usual language for firmware on boards such as Arduino, STM32 and ESP32 because it runs with little overhead. Get strong at pointers, structures, functions and memory, and learn to follow a coding standard such as BARR-C.

resources.title: Problem Solving through Programming in C – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)
BARR-C:2018 Embedded C Coding Standard (free PDF)

nodes.proof: A small C library (for example a ring buffer) with tests, written to follow BARR-C rules.

sources.title: C++ vs. C: when to use each – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Microcontroller basics with Arduino or Pico
nodes.summary: Start on a beginner board: blink an LED, read buttons and analog sensors, and print over serial. Then move to the Raspberry Pi Pico C SDK to work closer to the hardware with CMake and plain C.

resources.title: Getting Started with Arduino – Arduino Docs
The C/C++ SDK – Raspberry Pi Documentation

nodes.proof: Three small sketches (digital input, analog read, serial output) on one board, with photos and code on GitHub.

sources.title: The C/C++ SDK – Raspberry Pi Documentation

nodes.title: Interrupts and ARM Cortex-M basics
nodes.summary: Learn how a Cortex-M processor handles exceptions and interrupts through the NVIC: priorities, the vector table and handler mode. This is how real firmware reacts to timers, buttons and peripherals without wasting time polling.

resources.title: Embedded System Design with ARM – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)
Cortex-M0+ Devices Generic User Guide – Arm

nodes.proof: A timer interrupt that toggles an LED while the main loop does other work, with notes on how you set the priority.

sources.title: Exception handling and prioritization – Arm Cortex-M4 TRM
Embedded System Design with ARM – NPTEL

nodes.title: UART, I2C and SPI
nodes.summary: Most sensors and displays talk over UART, I2C or SPI. Learn how each one works, read a sensor datasheet, and use your chip's peripheral drivers. The NXP manual is the official I2C reference.

resources.title: UM10204 I2C-bus specification and user manual – NXP

nodes.proof: Read one I2C sensor and one SPI device on the same board, with a logic-analyser or serial-log screenshot.

sources.title: UM10204 I2C-bus specification and user manual – NXP
Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) – Linux kernel docs

nodes.title: ESP32 with ESP-IDF
nodes.summary: ESP-IDF is Espressif's official framework for the ESP32. Learn to set the target, build, flash and monitor with idf.py, and use its GPIO, I2C, SPI, UART and Wi-Fi APIs. Use the stable docs, not old versions.

resources.title: ESP-IDF versions – which docs to use

nodes.proof: An ESP-IDF project that reads a sensor and connects to Wi-Fi, built from the command line, with a README.

nodes.title: RTOS with FreeRTOS
nodes.summary: A real-time OS lets you split firmware into tasks. Learn tasks, priorities, queues, mutexes, semaphores and software timers in FreeRTOS. ESP-IDF includes FreeRTOS, so you can practise on the same ESP32.

resources.title: Mastering the FreeRTOS Real Time Kernel (free PDF)

nodes.proof: A three-task firmware (sensor, processing, output) that passes data through queues, with a diagram of the tasks.

nodes.title: MQTT and connecting devices
nodes.summary: MQTT is an OASIS-standard publish/subscribe messaging protocol. Learn topics, QoS levels and retained messages, then run the free Mosquitto broker locally and test with mosquitto_pub and mosquitto_sub.
nodes.proof: Your ESP32 publishes sensor readings to a local Mosquitto broker and reacts to a command topic.

nodes.title: Embedded Linux on Raspberry Pi
nodes.summary: Bigger devices run Linux. Learn the boot process, cross-compiling, using GPIO, I2C and SPI from Linux, and how kernel drivers fit in. Bootlin's free course and the Yocto Quick Build are good next steps.

resources.title: Raspberry Pi computer hardware – Raspberry Pi Documentation

nodes.proof: A Raspberry Pi program that reads an I2C or SPI sensor from Linux user space, with setup steps in a README.

sources.title: SPI userspace API (spidev) – Linux kernel docs

nodes.title: Project: sensor node with FreeRTOS and MQTT
nodes.summary: Build one complete device: an ESP32 reads an I2C sensor in a FreeRTOS task, publishes to MQTT over Wi-Fi, and a Raspberry Pi or laptop subscribes and logs the data. Document wiring, design and known limits.
nodes.proof: A public repo with code, a wiring diagram, a task diagram and a two-minute demo video of the device working.

nodes.title: Embedded interview preparation
nodes.summary: Revise C (pointers, memory, bit operations), interrupts, RTOS ideas such as tasks, queues and mutexes, and UART, I2C and SPI. Be ready to walk through your project's design and the bugs you fixed.

resources.title: Mastering the FreeRTOS Real Time Kernel (free PDF)
Employment Communication: A Lab-based Course – NPTEL

nodes.proof: A one-page summary of your project you can explain in five minutes, plus answers to 30 practice questions.
